notes: Every window of a followed task that is not a browser is listened to (Notepad, a settings box, File Explorer, an Office window), from the moment it is followed: a button, tick box, list entry, tab or menu entry a program presses there through Windows (UI Automation) gets the pointer on that thing.

A click a program makes with the mouse itself is followed in every window, also in an app you had open already. Windows gives such a press no device; your own mouse and touchpad always have one, so your own clicks are never taken for it.

Honest about whose click it was. In a window that is not the task's own nobody can say which program clicked: it is taken for the followed task most likely at work (an AI agent before a scheduled task) and the trace says (not its own window: taken for its click). With no followed task the trace still has a program nobody follows, with the program and the point.
Fixed on the way: the screen listener could fail to start when its thread was the first one to load COM.

What it cannot show: a press through Windows in an app you had open already that is not a followed window (no mouse, no news), a round option box in a Windows Forms program chosen that way, a box filled without the keyboard, and programs that tell Windows nothing (there only mouse clicks are followed). Firefox and command windows are not followed.

New: the agent pointer. When a program clicks with the mouse, in any app, a second pointer in another colour flies to the click, shows a ring and names the program: Terminal clicked here. It leaves 2.5 s after the last click.
